plate_findings.evidence: Ossification involving medial collateral ligament (MCL) as a Pellegrini–Stieda lesion.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Coronal T2WI MRI of the left knee shows evidence of ossification in the MCL region, consistent with the described Pellegrini-Stieda lesion, a related pathology for MCL conditions. B: Transverse PDWI MRI of the left knee demonstrates the presence of the Pellegrini-Stieda lesion, which involves the medial joint capsule. C: Sagittal T2WI MRI of the left knee confirms the presence of the Pellegrini-Stieda lesion, representing ossification of the medial structures.

According to the anteroposterior and lateral view of the x-ray, the cartilage wear area was mainly located in the anteromedial of the left knee (Figures 1A, B). The full-weight-bearing x-ray showed varus deformity of the left knee, and the intra-articular deformity occupied the main (Figure 1D). So, we conducted medial mobile-bearing unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (Oxford UKA, Zimmer Biomet, Warsaw, IN, United States) for this patient. findings.label: Pellegrini-Stieda calcification
findings.evidence: Bilateral Pellegrini-Stieda calcification of the MCL

panels.rationale: The radiograph explicitly shows bilateral heterotopic ossification (Pellegrini-Stieda calcification) located at the MCL of both knees, as supported by the caption and in-text evidence. This finding is linked to the evaluated disease.
panels.attribution_text: Maroc et al. Longitudinally Extensive Transverse Myelitis and Bilateral Pellegrini-Stieda Syndrome Coexisting in a Young Woman With Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: Report of a Rare Case.. Cureus 2025. doi:10.7759/cureus.88409. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Plain radiograph of both knees showing bilateral Pellegrini-Stieda calcification This anteroposterior view of both knees strikingly demonstrates distinct bilateral heterotopic ossification (white arrows) of the MCL, adjacent to the medial femoral condyles, a notable finding in this patient.
in_text_mentions: Given these new symptoms, both plain radiographs (Figure 2) and ultrasound examinations (Figure 3) of the knees were promptly conducted. These imaging modalities identified characteristic calcifications located at the MCL of both knees, definitively establishing the diagnosis of bilateral PSD.
